failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 3 query: 'What is the actual verification status of the claim that "the father of the Princess Charlotte of Lorraine has a descendant that includes Umberto II the a king of Italy"? Specifically: (1) Can the historical identity of Princess Charlotte of Lorraine be confirmed from the available passages? (2) Is her father identified in the passages? (3) Do the passages establish a documented genealogical connection between her father and Umberto II of Italy? (4) Which summary's assessment accurately reflects what the source passages actually contain?' This is a natural-language yes/no question bundled with multiple sub-questions rather than a targeted entity-based retrieval query.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 3 returned passages include 'Gilead (tribal group)' about Biblical tribal groups, 'Charlotte of Naples' (1479-1506) about Italian royalty unrelated to Lorraine, and 'Hanoverian princess' about George III's descendants. None of these are relevant to verifying the Princess Charlotte of Lorraine claim. The trace shows no explicit rejection of these irrelevant passages.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 3 query asks 'What is the actual verification status of the claim...? Specifically: (1) Can the historical identity of Princess Charlotte of Lorraine be confirmed from the available passages? (2) Is her father identified...' This re-asks questions already answered in hop 2, where passages [5] and [6] explicitly identified Charlotte de Lorraine-Armagnac as the daughter of Louis, Count of Armagnac, whose descendants include Umberto II. The query ignores the guidance from summary_2 that verification was complete.
